CONFIDENTIAL EMPLOYMENT OFFER LETTER Date: October 24, 2026 Candidate: Jonathan Mercer Position: Principal Distributed Systems Engineer Reporting To: Vice President of Engineering Dear Jonathan, We are delighted to extend this formal offer of employment with Readr Technologies Inc. This document details the terms, compensation structure, and contractual covenants of your engagement. 1. Compensation and Equity Grants

Your starting base salary will be $225,000 USD per annum, payable semi-monthly in accordance with standard payroll practices. Additionally, subject to approval by the Board of Directors, you will be granted an option to purchase 45,000 shares of Common Stock. These incentive options will vest over a 48-month period, with a 25% cliff after exactly 12 months of active service, followed by monthly equal tranches. 2. Annual Performance Bonus and Relocation Stipend

You will be eligible for an annual performance bonus with a target threshold of 20% of your base salary, calculated based on milestone delivery and system uptime metrics. You will also receive an immediate, non-recoverable relocation allowance of $15,000 USD to facilitate your transition to our Seattle engineering office. 3. Restrictive Covenants and Non-Compete Clauses

During the term of your employment and for a mandatory period of twelve (12) consecutive months following the termination of your employment for any reason, you shall not directly or indirectly engage in, perform services for, invest in, or consult with any competitive passage retrieval or deterministic indexing technology provider within North America and the European Economic Area. 4. Termination and Severance Provisions

In the event that your employment is terminated by the Company without Cause, you shall be entitled to receive four (4) months of continuous base salary continuation as severance, contingent upon your execution of an unreserved general liability release. Please indicate your acceptance of this offer by signing and returning this letter by November 15, 2026.

# Readr Deterministic Retrieval Architecture ## 1. Engine Specifications The Readr passage retrieval system replaces opaque probabilistic vector databases with an exact mathematical BM25 ranking engine written in pure Golang. The scoring parameters are locked to k1 = 1.5 and b = 0.75, with length normalization calculated dynamically against the corpus average document length (avgdl). ## 2. Ingestion Pipeline and Chunker

Incoming text streams are stripped of standard English stopwords using a fast in-memory map filter. Sentences are delimited along terminal punctuation boundaries (. ? !). When any individual paragraph exceeds 600 characters, it undergoes recursive sentence splitting to ensure chunks remain between 200 and 600 characters without stripping source words. ## 3. WebSocket Protocol Specs

Communication between the Next.js 16 frontend and the Go engine runs over a single full-duplex WebSocket connection mounted at `ws://localhost:3030/ws`. Heartbeat frames are exchanged via 25-second ping/pong cycles. All requests follow JSON-RPC 2.0 specifications. Prior to running passage ranking, the engine emits an intermediate `notifications/progress` frame with a progressToken and a status message reading "Scanning chunks...". ## 4. Minimum Confidence Guards To prevent hallucinated or spurious results, two mathematical guards are strictly enforced:

- Minimum confidence score threshold: 0.30 - Minimum keyword match ratio: 0.40 (at least 40% of non-stopword query tokens must appear verbatim in candidate passages) If no candidate chunk meets both criteria, the engine deterministically returns status `not_found`.
